subject: Music Production
title: Masking and Frequency Competition
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Masking and Frequency Competition.

hook.text: When two instruments play in the same frequency range, one can make the other nearly inaudible.

buildup.text: This psychoacoustic phenomenon is called masking, and it's a major challenge in dense mixes.

discovery.text: Louder sounds mask quieter ones nearby in frequency because the ear cannot separate them easily.

twist.text: A guitar and a vocal in the same range compete, even though they sound fine played separately.

climax.text: Producers use equalization to carve space for each instrument and reduce masking in a mix.

punchline.text: Instruments in the same range fight to be heard.

quiz.question: What causes frequency masking in a mix?
options: Too many effects on a track
Two instruments competing in the same frequency range
Recording at too high a volume
